title: AEF 1.0: the checkpoint decision function's input and output
description: READER (tolerant), derived from the writer schema by tools/derive_reader.py. Decide(input) -> output is pure: no I/O, no clock (the evaluation time is an input). Its rules are DEC-1 to DEC-5 and its vectors are in conformance/decision-vectors/. This schema is the output; $defs/input is the input.

outcome.description: expired (superseded, or a lane is stale); blocked (a blocking lane failed and is not waived); inconclusive (a lane is missing, not_measured or incomparable); approved_with_exceptions (otherwise, when an exception waived a lane); or approved (DEC-3).

lanes.description: Each input lane's status, in the input's order (DEC-2).

status.description: The lane's status under the decision rules (DEC-2).

blocking.description: Whether the lane blocks the release when it fails, as in the input (DEC-3).

axes.description: For incomparable: the comparability axes that differ.

reasons.description: Reason codes, so every implementation produces the same list: one per lane that did not pass, advisory-failed and waived included, in the input's lane order, each followed by exception-expired:<lane> when the lane failed and none of its exceptions is in force; then superseded:<version> when it applies; then outcome:<outcome> (DEC-2, DEC-4).

laneStatus.description: passed / failed: the lane's rule held or did not on its evidence. missing: no evidence for this exact version at the evaluation time (none, another version's, or evidence that did not exist yet). not_measured: the rule could not decide on the evidence, for example nothing was measured or a run is not eligible. incomparable: a comparison's runs differ on a required axis. stale: older than the lane's freshness at the evaluation time. waived: failed, with an exception in force at the evaluation time; only a failure is ever waived (DEC-2, LANE-1).

input.description: The decision function's input: the exact version, the evaluation time, an optional newer version, each lane's result, and any exceptions. At least one lane, no lane twice, and every exception for a lane of the input, expiring after it is granted (DEC-1).

evaluatedAt.description: The time the decision is made for. Freshness, future evidence and whether an exception is in force are judged against it (DEC-1, DEC-2).

supersededBy.description: A newer subject version known at the evaluation time, if any. When set and different from subjectVersion, the outcome is expired (DEC-3).

lanes.description: The lanes, at least one and none twice; the reasons follow this order (DEC-1, DEC-4).

blocking.description: Whether a failure of this lane blocks the release (DEC-3).

freshness.description: How old the lane's evidence may be. Without it, the lane never goes stale (DEC-2).

result.description: What the lane's rule gave on its evidence (computed from the runs, outside this function), or null when there is no evidence.

status.description: What the lane's rule gave: passed, failed, not_measured or incomparable. A status this version does not know reads as not_measured (DEC-2).

subjectVersion.description: The version the evidence was produced for.

oldestClosedAt.description: When the oldest run the lane's result relied on closed: freshness is measured from it.

axes.description: For incomparable: the axes that differ, in the order the rule lists them (LANE-6).

exceptions.description: Exceptions: a person's decision to accept a failed lane's risk until a time. One in force at evaluatedAt makes its failed lane waived; it never changes a missing, stale, not_measured or incomparable lane. A checkpoint records them in its decisionInput, so its signature covers them (DEC-1, DEC-2, CKP-5).

items.description: One exception. Each names a lane of this input and expires after it is granted, or the function refuses the input (DEC-1).

lane.description: The lane it applies to: a lane of this input, or the function refuses the input (DEC-1).

requirement.description: The external requirement id whose risk it accepts, shown beside the waived lane; it takes no part in the decision (DEC-1, DEC-2).

reason.description: Why the risk is accepted, shown beside the waived lane (DEC-1, DEC-2).

by.description: Who granted it. A claim: a reader shows its assurance only as far as it verified it; the checkpoint's signature says who recorded it (DEC-1, CKP-5, CKP-6).

at.description: When it was granted: it is in force from this time, inclusive (DEC-2, DEC-5).

expires.description: When it stops being in force: from this time on it waives nothing. Later than at, or the function refuses the input (DEC-1, DEC-2, CKP-10).
